name: car_sedan_fuel
source: PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7. Identical to data/vehicles/car_sedan.json (chassis geometry, suspension, tyres, steering, brake_system, aero, gearbox, differential, controllers all UNCHANGED - see that file's own 'source' field for their derivation) except: (1) the engine component's ref is data/engines/toyota_a25a_fks.json (2018 Toyota 2.5L A25A-FKS, EPA NVFEL Report 26781 - see that file's own 'source' field) in place of the generic i4_2l_na.json placeholder; (2) a fuel_tank component + fluid link were added; (3) the clutch capacity_nm was raised, IN THIS FILE ONLY (car_sedan.json itself is never edited). The real 2018 Camry's own 8-speed automatic transmission (U880E) is NOT modeled - this file keeps car_sedan.json's sedan_6mt 6-speed manual gearbox and manual_tcu controller unchanged, so gearing/shift behaviour here is a stand-in, not a Camry replica; only the engine and fuel system are the cited Camry unit. CLUTCH CAPACITY: car_sedan.json's own source field states its 300.0 N*m capacity was sized as '1.5 x engine peak torque' for the OLD i4_2l_na.json engine (peak WOT torque 200 N*m there). The new toyota_a25a_fks.json engine's MEASURED peak WOT torque is 232.04 N*m (at 4493.1 rpm, EPA NVFEL Report 26781 High Load Final sheet, pedal=100 row - see that engine file's own citation). Carrying the old 300.0 N*m forward would give only 300/232.04 = 1.293x, below car_sedan.json's own documented 'typical passenger-car reserve 1.3-1.8' range. Raised, using the SAME 1.5x convention car_sedan.json itself used: 232.04 * 1.5 = 348.06 N*m, rounded to the same round-number style as the original (300.0) -> 350.0 N*m (350.0/232.04 = 1.508x, inside the 1.3-1.8 range). static_factor (1.15) and the engagement_vs_pedal curve are unchanged from car_sedan.json - only capacity_nm differs. FUEL TANK: fuel = ../fuels/tier3_e10_cert.json (the EPA Tier 3 certification fuel toyota_a25a_fks.json's own fuel_map was measured on - required by PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7's 'a map's fuel must be the fuel it was measured on' rule; also present in that engine's fuels list). Capacity CITED: fueleconomy.gov (US DOE/EPA joint fuel-economy site, https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/Find.do?action=sbs&id=38883), '2018 Toyota Camry LE/SE' (4-cylinder, the trim this engine actually ships in): 'Tank Size: 16.0 gallons' (US gallons). DERIVED capacity_kg: 16.0 US gal * 3.785411784 L/gal (exact US-gallon-to-litre conversion) = 60.566588544 L; 60.566588544 L * 0.74326 kg/L (tier3_e10_cert.json's own density_kg_m3=743.26, i.e. 0.74326 kg/L) = 45.016722541... kg, rounded to 45.02 kg. initial_kg = capacity_kg (a full tank) = 45.02. fluid link tank.out -> engine.fuel per docs/data_formats/vehicle.md / tests/support/fixtures/vehicle_tank_sedan.json's established syntax; this is the only engine/fuel_tank pairing in the vehicle (no fluid ambiguity).
